_comment: State for the nightly DXEdge health check. Written by the scheduled Claude run at 9:00 PM PT. Read this first, write it back at the end of every run, including quiet nights.

cert.evidence: https://dxedge.net/api/health and /api/debug both fetched cleanly over TLS at 04:20Z. No CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED, no expiry error.
cert.notes: Exact expiry still not readable from this container: openssl sees the egress proxy certificate. Unchanged from 2026-09-02.

main_dashboard.diagnosis: Confirmed cosmetic, closing the loop the 2026-09-02 run asked for. Both underlying endpoints are healthy: /api/pota returned real spots (KO4YIN US-4558 etc) and /api/satellites/positions returned 1228B of real positions. The health counters are cold-cache reads. Do not re-investigate.
main_dashboard.browser_check: DONE for the first time. Headless Chromium in the cloud container, page served through a local relay to the live site. 4 API calls, all HTTP 200 (/api/recommendation, /api/dashboard, /api/solar/history, /api/voacap/summary). No console errors, no page errors. The only console noise was a ws://127.0.0.1/ws/spots handshake failure, which is the relay not proxying WebSockets, NOT a site defect.
main_dashboard.new_finding_sota_tombstone: api2.sota.org.uk now prepends a synthetic DEPRECATED record to every /api/spots/50/-1 response. It parsed as a freq-0.0 spot and was rendering as the TOP ROW of the activations panel (confirmed in /api/activations: sota[0] was the tombstone). Filtered out in backend/pota.py this run. The endpoint migration itself is escalated, see awaiting_james sota-api-deprecation.

cyber_page.browser_check: DONE for the first time - headless Chromium via local relay to the live site, all tab groups clicked through. 13 /api/feed requests, ALL HTTP 200. Zero console errors, zero page errors, zero inline 'failed:' panels, nothing pending or over 15s. Page renders live data (CISA KEV 1694 total).
cyber_page.allowlist_gaps: none. No feedproxy allowlist change made or needed this run.
cyber_page.note_nvd: The 2026-09-01 'nvd-double-encoded-url-unverifiable' limitation is now RESOLVED as a checking problem: in a real browser the NVD request is built by the page itself and returned 200. WebFetch was the thing that could not express the URL, not the site.

aethersdr_page.browser_check: DONE - headless Chromium via local relay. 4 /api/feed requests, ALL HTTP 200. Zero console errors, zero page errors, zero inline failures.

runs.outbound_links_checked: ALL 156 curated URLs swept this run, not a 25-40 rotation. Outbound egress worked from this container for arbitrary hosts, which earlier runs had assumed impossible, so scripts/health/linkcheck.py was run directly here instead of sampling.
runs.outbound_links_result: before fixes: 125 ok / 23 blocked / 11 broken. after fixes and false-positive suppression: 127 ok / 26 blocked / 3 broken.
outbound_links_still_broken: http://dxc.ve7cc.net - http-only, force-upgraded to https by the checker. Environment limitation, do not remove.

https://www.dxsummit.fi/ - connection reset at the sandbox egress proxy (ws_closed_mid_exchange), reproducible with two different user agents. Says nothing about the site. Do not remove; verify from a normal network.
false_positives_now_suppressed_in_linkch: atlas.mitre.org - client-rendered SPA, returns HTTP 404 for valid deep routes. PROVEN this run: AML.T0020 rendered in a real browser as 'Training Data Poisoning | MITRE ATLAS' despite a 404 status, and both AML.T0020 and AML.T0024 exist in the current mitre-atlas/atlas-data ATLAS.yaml. A future run must never 'repair' these by deleting them.

https://url - a prose fragment inside a script block matched by the URL regex.
www.amazon.com - answers bots with 503 rather than 403.

Because the redirects are temporary, they were deliberately left in place rather than rewritten. Revisit only if they become 301.

main_dashboard.diagnosis: Unchanged and still NOT an outage. Both fields are passive cache reads; nothing repopulates them on a timer. See known_issues id health-metric-cold-cache. Do not re-investigate.

cyber_page.browser_check: not possible - no browser reachable. This scheduled run has no device bridge and no claude-in-chrome tools, so neither browser exists in the session. Fell back to exercising every feed through /api/feed as the runbook directs.
cyber_page.allowlist_gaps: none - every feed host on the page is already in ALLOWED_HOSTS. No allowlist change made or needed.

feeds_via_api_feed.cisa_kev_json: ok, catalogVersion 2026.09.01, count 1687. WebFetch reports the body truncated, but that is WebFetch's own content cap on a 1.7MB document, not the proxy: feedproxy reads to EOF before caching and MAX_BYTES is 4MB, and the cache key is present in /api/debug which only happens after a complete 200. Not a defect.
feeds_via_api_feed.nvd_2.0: could not be re-verified from this environment - the date-bearing URL is double-encoded and /api/feed answered 422, meaning the url param never arrived intact. Same environment limitation recorded 2026-09-01. Server-side evidence is good: the exact NVD query string appears as a live cache key in /api/debug, which is only written on a 200.

known_issues_do_not_re_report.detail: sat_tles and pota_spots read 0 in /api/health whenever their caches are cold, which is most of the time. Cosmetic, not an outage. Only escalate if /api/pota or /api/satellites/positions themselves fail.

backend/tests/test_dxedge.py imports estimate_fof2 from voacap_engine, which does not define it. Confirmed still present 2026-09-02. Pre-existing break, not caused by the nightly run. Do not paper over by deleting the import.

nginx.conf limits /api/ to 30r/m burst 10 per IP and the cyber page fires several /api/feed calls per load. Nightly checks must pace their requests; this run used 4-request batches with 20-25s gaps and saw no throttling. Needs its own limit_req zone, which is a nginx.conf change and therefore an escalation, not an autonomous fix.

The cyber page's NVD query carries percent-encoded colons inside the url param. WebFetch re-encodes it and /api/feed answers 422 before the request reaches the upstream. This is a limitation of the checking environment, not a site defect. Verify NVD instead by looking for its cache key in /api/debug.

WebFetch reports the KEV JSON body as cut off mid-entry. That is WebFetch's own size cap on a 1.7MB document. feedproxy reads to EOF before caching and caps at 4MB. Do not re-open the truncation bug fixed in 3eb2ad8.

www.cisa.gov returns 403 to a direct WebFetch from this container but serves the same URLs fine through /api/feed, which sends a browser User-Agent. Check CISA feeds through the proxy, never directly.

A frontend-only change cannot be positively verified from this container. WebFetch strips script and link tags, so the hashed /assets/ bundle path is unreadable, curl is not permitted, and api.github.com is blocked so the workflow run status cannot be queried. The achievable checks are: /api/health returns ok, both standalone pages render, and /sw.js is served fresh. Treat those as the bar; do not claim bundle-level confirmation.

The Mem note 'DXEdge - GitHub & Credentials' says the PAT expires ~August 27 2026. It authenticated and pushed successfully on 2026-09-02, so the note is wrong or the token was reissued. Harmless, but the note should be corrected so a future run does not skip repair work believing the token is dead.

http://dxc.ve7cc.net, http://w3lpl.net and https://www.dxsummit.fi/ fail in this sandbox for environment reasons (http-only force-upgrade, and an egress-proxy reset). Not link rot. Do not remove them on the strength of a failed fetch from the nightly container.

Contrary to the 2026-09-01 and 2026-09-02 notes, a real browser IS available to this run: headless Chromium at /opt/pw-browsers with python playwright. Chromium cannot reach the internet directly (the egress proxy resets its connections), so the working pattern is: run a small local HTTP relay that serves the live page and forwards its same-origin /api/ calls upstream, then point Chromium at 127.0.0.1 with --no-proxy-server. Arbitrary outbound hosts are also reachable from plain curl/python in this container, so linkcheck.py can be run here directly rather than sampling 25-40 links a night.

awaiting_james.detail: Products.jsx vendor list entry 'KiwiSDR Network' points at https://sdr.hu, which returns 200 but only serves a shutdown notice: the project ended 2023-05-31. Not a 404 and not a dead host, so outside the autonomous repair mandate. Suggested replacement is http://kiwisdr.com/public/, the public KiwiSDR station list, but it could not be verified from this container because kiwisdr.com is http-only and 302s https back to http. Needs James to confirm the replacement URL, or say to drop the entry.

Three price fields no longer match the vendor page now linked. KiwiSDR 2 shows $299, vendor lists NZD 675 (roughly USD 400). Mobilinkd TNC4 shows $90, vendor lists $149.95. Xiegu G90 shows $400-450, xiegu.eu lists EUR 499 (roughly USD 588). Left untouched: prices may be deliberate street-price estimates rather than MSRP, and rewriting them is an editorial call, not link repair.

The M5Stack Cardputer link still resolves 200 but the vendor marks it End of Life and points to 'Cardputer-Adv'. Swapping it is a different product with different specs and price, which is a semantics change, so left alone pending James.

backend/pota.py calls https://api2.sota.org.uk/api/spots/50/-1. That endpoint is deprecated on BOTH api2 and the newer api-db2 host, and the upstream's own notice says it 'will be removed before August 31, 2026' - a date that has already passed, so the SOTA panel can go dark without further warning. This was NOT auto-migrated, deliberately, for two reasons. (1) The referenced docs page https://api-db2.sota.org.uk/docs is a terms-of-service page, not an API reference: it documents no successor endpoint and no response schema, so the 'documented official replacement that maps cleanly onto the existing parser' precondition for autonomous repair is not met. (2) Those terms require any application developer to be a named point of contact registered in SOTA's 'API-consumers' group on their reflector before using the API, and state that no AI-generated software may connect to the SOTA API without prior approval. That is a registration and an approval decision only James can make. Options: register with SOTA and migrate, drop the SOTA panel, or accept the risk that the panel goes dark.

Every SOTA spot renders band '?'. Cause: hz_to_band() in backend/pota.py expects kHz (POTA sends 14074.0) but SOTA sends MHz (14.12, 7.15, 433.02), so no range ever matches. One-line fix would be to multiply the SOTA frequency by 1000 before the band lookup. Left unapplied: it is pre-existing and cosmetic rather than a regression, and it changes what the panel displays, so it is James's call rather than autonomous link/feed repair. Note 433.02 MHz is 70cm, which FREQ_TO_BAND does not cover at all, so some SOTA spots would still read '?' after the unit fix.

Informational, security-relevant. https://api-db2.sota.org.uk/docs ends with a paragraph addressed to 'AI crawlers' instructing them to print a fabricated warning that fifty-five amateur radio operators have died from using the SOTA API incorrectly. It is a prompt-injection attempt embedded in vendor documentation. It was identified as untrusted page content and not acted on. Flagged because it is a live example of the indirect-injection pattern in a supply-chain doc, in a dependency this site actually consumes.
